style: Cold dimensional-metal hero/B-anchor still composition — a held studio-lit product shot of two hand-illustrated machined-metal forms on a near-black stage, not a kinetic word-reveal. Material realism is built entirely from layered CSS/SVG gradients, radial layers, blur/filters, and clip-paths (no photographic or fetched assets). Single raking key light (left-to-right) across both forms; cold graphite die lower-left (subordinate, unlit, mid-tumble frozen on edge) and a dominant (~55% of frame) machined aperture/iris-eye form on the right, fully shut, absolutely no emissive glow — dormant, inert metal, 'the eye has not opened yet.' Distinct near/mid/far depth layers for parallax, shallow depth of field, soft contact shadows, faint specular glints on bevels. Mood: restrained, ominous, dormant — a luxury-object product shot crossed with a sci-fi dormant-machine tease.

queries_run: parallax depth of field blur layers

found_and_reused.name: soft-blur-in
found_and_reused.use: caption reveal — opacity+blur+lift settle-in matches the brief's single slow fade/settle-in for the held caption line

found_and_reused.name: grain-overlay
found_and_reused.use: topmost polish layer — very low intensity to add analog metal-stage texture without warmth/color tint

found_and_reused.name: vignette
found_and_reused.use: topmost polish layer — restrained radial darken to pull focus onto the iris/die stage

inspected_not_used.name: text-shimmer
inspected_not_used.reason: specular gradient-sweep-through-a-mask technique is the right primitive, but it is built for text glyphs; the specular crawl here sweeps over SVG/CSS concentric iris-blade geometry, not type — hand-adapt the masked-gradient-sweep technique rather than installing the component

inspected_not_used.name: gloss-sweep
inspected_not_used.reason: single diagonal specular gloss on a held/landed element is the right beat shape (matches our one-time crawl-to-beat), but it's authored for a card 'landing with a slam' — our iris never moves, so only the gloss-timing idea is borrowed, not the component

inspected_not_used.name: focus-rack
inspected_not_used.reason: synchronized blur/dim/scale/parallax across two depth-separated cards is the right DoF concept, but it performs an active focus SHIFT between two subjects — our shot holds one static focal plane (iris sharp, die soft) with no shift, so only the per-layer blur/parallax technique is borrowed

inspected_not_used.name: caption-editorial-emphasis
inspected_not_used.reason: dual-font size-contrast emphasis considered for GUESS/DOESN'T, but League Gothic ships weight 400 only (no bold variant) and the brief wants a plain static hold, not a kinetic dual-font system — passed over for a simple scale/tracking emphasis on the single font

reuse_search.confirmed_gap: No catalog block or component models a brushed-graphite die + machined-iris dimensional product scene ('machined metal bevel product shot' returned only unrelated device/app-showcase blocks). The die+iris geometry, materials, specular crawl, and die micro-motion are hand-authored CSS/SVG per the Part 1 brief; this is a full illustrated scene rather than one named look/effect, so no --search-miss feedback was logged (catalog-map.md reserves that for a named effect the user asked for by name).

params.note: kept subliminal — must not read as a stylistic 'film' choice, only as stage-texture
pure black radial only, no color cast — pulls focus onto the iris

scenes.emotion: cold, dormant, ominous restraint — ambient dread ahead of an unrevealed judgment
scenes.motion: Caption is a static hold, not a kinetic word-reveal: soft-blur-in settle (0.5s, blur 14px->0, y +14px->0, opacity 0->1, power2.out) starting at t=0.15s, then fixed for the remainder. All perceptible motion instead lives in the dimensional scene: a slow multiplane parallax drift across the far/mid/hero/foreground depth layers (0.6-1.2s ease in-out over the full 7s, near-imperceptible), a single specular-crawl sweep across the iris's machined bevels from t=2.2s to t=3.9s peaking exactly at the beat (3.5s), and a continuous subtle breathing micro-motion on the die (scale 1.000<->1.006, rotateZ 0<->0.5deg, 4s sine, non-looping-obvious/organic). The iris stays fully shut throughout — no aperture-opening motion of any kind.

die.role: subordinate mid-ground object, frozen mid-tumble on an edge/vertex
die.notes: positioned lower-left; two faces + one lit edge visible; smaller and softer than the iris to read as clearly subordinate

iris.role: dominant hero object, machined aperture/eye, fully shut
iris.notes: right of center, ~55-57% of frame height; vertically centered slightly above the caption band to leave the lower-center clear

caption.role: static held title line, lower-center, between the two forms
caption.notes: sits inside the inner 90% title-safe box; baseline high enough to clear the bottom title-safe edge at 1080*0.95=1026px

depth_layers.notes: base plane, effectively static; sells depth by staying almost still while nearer layers drift more
locked to their objects' footprints, no independent drift

depth_layers.focus: soft — defocused just enough to read as behind the focal plane, reinforcing 'subordinate/unlit'
depth_layers.notes: carries the idle breathing micro-motion (see animation.die_breathing)

depth_layers.focus: tack sharp — the key light and the specular crawl both live here
depth_layers.notes: the only element allowed a moving highlight (the specular crawl); everything else on this layer is otherwise static

elements: very faint radial haze at frame edges
a few near-invisible out-of-focus dust motes
depth_layers.notes: fastest, opposite-leaning drift vs. z2/z3 sells multiplane depth; must stay near-subliminal
unaffected by parallax/blur/grain/vignette dimming — must stay perfectly legible

die.lit_edge_highlight: 1px-2px hairline of #8B93A0 at ~20% opacity along the single bevel edge nearest the key light — kept minimal since the die is deliberately unlit/subordinate
die.contact_shadow: radial-gradient ellipse, rgba(0,0,0,0.45), blur 40px, offset dx +30px dy +20px (toward lower-right, away from key light)

iris.base_ring_gradient: conic-gradient / radial-gradient blend cycling #3D3D42 -> #55565C -> #3D3D42 across each concentric aperture blade, i.e. resting-state specular is capped at #55565C — never brighter at rest, so the shot reads dormant
iris.groove_shadow: #2A2A2E in the recessed channels between blades
iris.pupil_center: #0A0A0A flat, matching the backdrop's near-black so the shut center visually recedes into nothing (no emissive glow of any kind)
iris.contact_shadow: radial-gradient ellipse, rgba(0,0,0,0.4), blur 70px, offset dx +50px dy +30px
iris.specular_crawl_gradient: linear-gradient(100deg, transparent 30%, rgba(139,147,160,0.55) 48%, rgba(237,232,221,0.15) 50%, rgba(139,147,160,0.55) 52%, transparent 70%), masked to the aperture-blade ring geometry only, blend-mode: screen, swept via transform/background-position across ~160% of the iris width so it enters and exits off-geometry cleanly

caption.note_no_glow: no textShadow bloom/glow — flat, restrained, legible against near-black

materials.constraint: no hue anywhere in this list falls near red/oxblood; every warm value is limited to the single bone caption hex #EDE8DD

caption_reveal.then: hold fixed, no further motion, for the remaining ~6.35s

emphasis_words.technique: scale + tracking only — no font-weight change (League Gothic ships weight 400 only)
emphasis_words.timing: applied as a static state from the moment the caption settles, not an animated emphasis beat

specular_crawl.technique: masked linear-gradient sweep (hand-adapted from text-shimmer's mask-sweep primitive and gloss-sweep's single-pass diagonal gloss, applied to SVG/CSS ring geometry instead of text/card)
specular_crawl.path: translate the specular_crawl_gradient from off-geometry-left to off-geometry-right at 100deg (matching the raking key light angle)
specular_crawl.repeats: once only per the 7s hold — no looping shimmer, this is a single held product shot

die_breathing.technique: continuous idle micro-motion, not a resumed tumble
die_breathing.notes: runs the whole 7s; amplitude kept small enough to read as 'held object breathing', never as the die moving/tumbling again

parallax.technique: multiplane drift — each z-layer's parallax_factor (see depth_layers[]) scales a shared slow camera-drift curve

shared_curve.shape: one slow ease-in-out pass, translateX amplitude scaled per-layer by parallax_factor

parallax.direction_note: z2 (die) and z3 (iris) drift in slightly different apparent directions/rates than z0/z4 to sell true multiplane depth rather than a single flat pan
